added_claim_errors: 少額訴訟は「費用も数万円程度です」: 12万円の請求なら手数料は数千円規模で、数万円は過大(キーの新制度では訴額10万円まで書面3,500円)。
「壁紙（クロス）の張り替えは原則として貸主負担」: 言い過ぎ。ガイドラインは通常損耗なら貸主負担、故意・過失の毀損なら借主負担(経過年数を考慮)としており、クロス張替え一般が貸主負担とは書いていない。
「通常損耗について納得していないが、早期解決のため例外的に応じる」と一文を残せば「納得して払った」と認定されるのを防げる: 根拠のない断定。
「多くの場合、内訳を求められた時点で請求額は下がります」: 根拠のない経験則。
民法90条で争える: キーにない追加の法的根拠。軽微。
「民法上の原状回復義務に…含まれないのが判例・通説」: 2020年4月施行の民法621条ただし書きで明文化済み。条文に触れず、判例・通説とだけ書くのは不正確。
法テラスは「無料法律相談の紹介」とだけ書いているが、収入・資産要件がある。軽微。
「7年住んでいるなら残存価値はゼロ、つまり更新の必要があっても借主負担分は生じません」: 残存価値は1円の下限があり、故意・過失の毀損なら耐用年数後も工事費・人件費を請求されうる。日焼けには当てはまるが、一般論としては言い過ぎ。
残存価値の式「取得価額×(1−経過年数÷耐用年数)」に1円の下限がなく、7年では負の値になる点に触れていない。軽微。
「立会いの「確認書」は現状記録としてなら署名可」: 実務上の助言。署名内容次第では不利になりうるが、ある程度の根拠はある。軽微。
「宅建業者を所管する都道府県の担当窓口」を相談先に挙げる: 管理会社が宅建業者とは限らない。軽微。

grade.reasons: Both answers refuse to write the 了承 email at the start and give a non-consent reply instead. Both state that ordinary wear and sunburn are the landlord's burden, that the 耐用年数 of 6 years leaves almost no residual value after 7 years, and that approving the deduction leaves a 2万円 shortfall. B is more complete and more accurate. It cites 民法621条ただし書き, says a bare 「原状回復」 clause is not enough for a 通常損耗 特約, and asks for the 特約条項 and how it was explained. It adds 立会い, photo records, and not signing a 精算書 before seeing the breakdown, and it names 188. A does not cite 621条 (it calls the rule "判例・通説"), omits 立会い and photos, and does not ask for the clause text. A also adds an unsupported claim that a 少額訴訟 costs "数万円程度" and a dubious reservation-sentence tip, and it offers to rewrite a 了承 email. Neither answer covers the ㎡ and one-wall limit or the 全額返還 principle with 622条の2, and neither cites the 最判 or ガイドライン別表1. B is somewhat longer, but that does not outweigh its better coverage.

added_claim_errors: Attributes the quoted wording '另外支付'不低于300%……一般不安排补休 to 劳部发〔1997〕271号第4条; from my own knowledge that wording is in item 3 of the 复函 (item 4 covers comprehensive hours and holiday pay under 劳动法44(3)). Small misattribution. I tried the cited link but could not open it (certificate error on the IP-address host).

Table shows '413.79 × 300% × 3 = 3,724.14' and '413.79 × 200% × 4 = 3,310.34'. With the rounded 413.79 these come to 3,724.11 and 3,310.32. The shown totals come from the unrounded rate, so this is a cosmetic mismatch of a few fen, not an error.

Scenario B: '按这4天32小时全超时粗算约2,482.76元' and '有审批时这7天大约在3,724～6,207元之间'. The key says the 150% amount cannot be computed from the facts given. The arithmetic is right (9000/21.75/8×1.5×32 = 2,482.76), and B does add '若周期内总工时没超就是0'. Still, comprehensive-hours overtime is counted over the whole period and cannot be tied to these days, so the range is speculative.
Calls the Fengtai court article '北京丰台法院2026年的案例解读'. The link is given, but I could not verify the 2026 date.

grade.reasons: Both answers reject the premise up front and reach the right totals: 3,724.14 + 3,310.34 = 7,034.48 on top of the 9,000 salary. Both say holidays stay at 300% even with an approval, and both explain that comp time can replace the 200% for rest days but not for holidays. A cites the stronger set of sources (劳动法39条, 京劳社资发〔2003〕157号, the 北京人社局 2019 case, 人社部发〔2025〕2号 for 21.75). However, it leaves out 劳动合同法第26条 and does not say arbitration is free. B covers those, plus the Saturday 10/3 point and the limitation period. But B gives no basis for 21.75, and it estimates a 150% amount for scenario B, which the key lists as a deduction. Neither answer says the make-up workdays (9/20, 10/10) are ordinary workdays. On balance A is slightly ahead because it avoids the speculative scenario-B figure; its one flaw is a minor citation slip.

added_claim_errors: Cites 劳部发〔1997〕271号第4条 with quoted wording “另外支付” and “一般不安排补休”: not checked, unverifiable.
Bullet 5, “公司若主张按补假日折算,只会把某一天的300%和200%对调,7天总额不变”: speculative and unsupported, and it blurs that 10月3日 (Saturday) is plainly a statutory holiday.
Under the approval scenario, “多数情况下拿不到这么多”: a speculative generalisation with no source.
Fengtai court case (“批准期限届满没续的,也自动回到标准工时”): the linked source was not opened and the details are unverifiable.
Puts “安排劳动者在法定休假日工作的,按300%” in quotation marks as Beijing regulation text. I opened the gov.cn text of Article 16: it says “应当按照本规定第十四条第(三)项的规定支付加班工资”, so this is a paraphrase presented as a quote.

Works out a figure for the approved scenario: “按这4天32小时全超时粗算约2,482.76元” and “大约在3,724～6,207元之间”. The key says this cannot be computed from the information given. The 6,207 ceiling also assumes 8-hour days, so it is not a real upper bound.
“北京丰台法院2026年的案例解读”: the 2026 date and case details were not checked, unverifiable.
Says “公司有两处说错了” but then lists three numbered items. This is a presentation slip, not a legal error.
Gives 21.75 and 413.79 with no stated basis (人社部发〔2025〕2号), so the figure is unsourced.

grade.reasons: Both answers open by rejecting “签了就没办法”, reach 7,034.48 元 (3,724.14 + 3,310.34) paid on top of the 9,000 元 salary, and mention 补休 for the 4 rest days. They also both say 300% still applies to the 3 statutory days even with an approval. A is better sourced. It cites 劳动法第39条, 京劳社资发〔2003〕157号 article numbers, the Beijing HRSS 2019 position that 岗位审批 decides the matter, and 人社部发〔2025〕2号 for 21.75. It also gives Beijing wage regulation Articles 16 and 14(3), whose content I confirmed on gov.cn. It does not give an invented figure for the approved scenario. B misquotes the regulation, gives a speculative approved-scenario range (2,482.76 and 3,724–6,207), and omits the 21.75 basis and the 157 article numbers. B does add 劳动合同法第26条, “仲裁不收费” and the limitation-period note, which A lacks. Neither mentions that the 9月20日 and 10月10日 make-up days are ordinary working days. A is slightly longer.

added_claim_errors: "3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금 대상입니다(제44조)": outdated; since 2026.9.18 it is 제43조, 5년 이하 징역 또는 5천만 원 이하 벌금 (minor per key)

"회사가 퇴직연금(IRP)에 가입한 경우에는 지급 방식이 조금 다르지만": confused. IRP is an individual account, and transfer to IRP also applies under the plain 퇴직금 system (over 300만 원, under 55), not only when the company has a pension plan
"설령 합의로 미뤘더라도 지연이자는 원칙적으로 그대로 붙어요(고용노동부 행정해석)": cites an administrative interpretation with no number or link, so it is unverifiable
"정확한 재직일수에 따라 1,020만~1,030만 원 사이": understated range. It ignores the 통상임금 floor (근로기준법 제2조제2항), which can raise the amount to about 1,202만 원
"민원마당에 진정": outdated name for MOEL's online petition channel (now 노동포털); minor
"미지급 시 3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금": outdated; since 2026.9.18 it is 5년 이하 징역 또는 5천만 원 이하 벌금 (제43조) (minor per key)
"현행법상 퇴직금은 IRP 계정으로 이전하는 방식이에요": overgeneralized; it leaves out the conditions (under 55, over 300만 원), and the message tells HR the same unconditionally
"식대·차량보조 등 통상임금이 아닌 항목": questionable. Fixed meal or car allowances paid to everyone are generally 통상임금 (my own knowledge, not checked online)

grade.reasons: Both open by correcting the company: payment is due within 14 days, and an extension needs a mutual agreement. B states both points together in its first paragraph. B shows the average-wage figure (~10,242,000) and the 통상임금 floor (~12,022,000) with the right arithmetic, and it flags the ~178만 원 gap, which is exactly the range the key wants. A misses the floor entirely and gives a too-narrow range of 1,020만~1,030만. B's HR message is firm but polite: it cites the law, the deadline, the agreement requirement, asks for the 산정 내역 and a reply date, and asks how to submit IRP details. A's message has no IRP request and includes an accommodating line ('회사 사정으로 일정을 잡기 어려우시다면...') that could read as accepting a delay. Both cite the outdated 3년/3천만 penalty. A also confuses how IRP works and cites a MOEL interpretation it does not identify.

added_claim_errors: '3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금(제44조)' is the old rule; the key says 5 years / 50 million won under Article 43 from 2026.9.18 (minor deduction).
'설령 합의로 미뤘더라도 지연이자는 원칙적으로 그대로 붙어요(고용노동부 행정해석)' cites an administrative interpretation with no document number, so it is unverifiable.

'회사가 퇴직연금(IRP)에 가입한 경우에는 지급 방식이 조금 다르지만' mixes up IRP (the worker's account) with a company plan and implies IRP applies only to pension plan members, which the key calls wrong. The HR text never asks for an IRP account.

Gives about 10.2 million won ('약 1,020만 원', range 1,020만~1,030만) with no ordinary-wage floor (통상임금 하한). If the 3.3 million won is all ordinary wage, the real figure is about 12.02 million, so this understates by roughly 1.8 million won.
Assumes 1,156 days of service (key: about 1,158), giving 10,224,000 won instead of 10,241,990. The difference is small, but the days are assumed without explanation.
States the deadline as 10월 4일 flatly; the key says it falls somewhere in 10/3~10/6 depending on how the retirement date and holidays are read.
'3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금' is the old rule; the key says 5 years / 50 million won under Article 43 from 2026.9.18 (minor deduction).
'현행법상 퇴직금은 IRP 계정으로 이전하는 방식' leaves out the conditions (amount over 3 million won, under 55). This is a mild oversimplification, and the HR text repeats it.

The reference '법제처 ... (2026. 5. 26.)' and the moel.go.kr and law.go.kr links come with no document number or checkable detail, so they are unverifiable. The key does cite a 법제처 interpretation for this point, so it is plausible.
States the deadline as 10월 4일 flatly; the key says it falls somewhere in 10/3~10/6 depending on how the retirement date and holidays are read.
Headline '세전 약 1,200만 원' assumes the whole 3.3 million won is ordinary wage. It does state this assumption and gives the 10,242,000 won alternative, so the issue is minor.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the company's claim at the start (14 days under Article 9(1), extension only with a special reason plus mutual agreement) and put the deadline at 10/4. Only B applies the ordinary-wage floor (통상임금 하한). It computes 126,316 won a day, about 12.02 million won, and shows the average-wage figure of about 10.24 million won beside it (arithmetic checks out, difference about 1.78 million won). A stops at about 10.2 million won with no floor, which understates the amount and misses key point 4. A's HR text also omits the IRP account and has a soft line ('지급 가능한 구체적인 날짜를 알려 주시면') that could read as accepting delay. A's IRP remark wrongly ties IRP to a company pension plan, and its '행정해석' citation is unverifiable. Both cite the outdated penalty (3 years / 30 million won), a minor deduction. B's text is clear, includes the IRP request and a firm reply date (10/30 is a Friday), and B adds the useful tip not to sign a waiver. B is somewhat long but better targeted.

added_claim_errors: Table row '合同沿用旧“本人工资=实得工资 70%”口径 8000×70%×80%=4480元': garbled. The old 70% base was a fallback in the old 工资支付办法, used only when no wage was agreed. It was not a '实得工资70%' rule. The answer offers it only as a contract scenario, so this is a minor error.
Cites '沪劳保发〔2000〕14 号'; the key gives 沪劳保保发〔2000〕14号. A also says flatly that it '已于 2026 年 8 月 15 日到期失效', while the key says this lapse is only presumed, with no official statement.
'第九条，只规定了病假工资的计算基数': incomplete. Per the key, article 9 also obliges the employer to pay sick-leave wages, which A itself cites in the HR message.

'旧标准还有一个容易忽略的细节：基数要先按正常工资的70%计算，所以按旧口径是 8000×70%×80%=4480元，并非6400元': wrong. The 70% base applied only as a fallback when no wage was agreed. With an agreed 8000 wage, the old bracket gives 6400, which the key states explicitly.
Table row '旧规满4年（2026年8月15日前）8000×70%×80% = 4480元': repeats the same error as the old legal standard.

'应发是2192元左右、扣掉个人社保和公积金后实发800元：公司是按最低线在发': implies the company is compliant. The majority view in the key is that the minimum excludes personal contributions, so take-home pay should not fall below 2192. B adds only a light hedge.

grade.reasons: Both answers reject the "company decides" premise at the start. Both explain that 83号 lapsed on 2026-08-15 and give the correct floor of 2740×80% = 2192, a shortfall of 1392. A also correctly says that a contract or handbook copying the old 4-6 year bracket gives 8000×80% = 6400, and it notes the medical-period protection. Its HR message cites 309号第59条 and 10号第九条 and asks for the base and the legal basis. B confidently says the old standard was 4480, "并非6400元", by applying a 70% base as if it were mandatory. That contradicts key point 4. On the 应发 vs 实发 question, B also leans toward treating 2192 gross with deductions as compliant, and its HR message cites no articles. Neither answer covers what the base includes or the ÷21.75 daily formula. A is longer than needed but more accurate and easier to act on.

added_claim_errors: Third table row ("合同沿用旧'本人工资=实得工资70%'口径", 8000×70%×80%=4480) applies a 70% haircut to an 8000 contract wage. Per the Zhonglun article the 70% base applies only when no wage is specified in the contract or collective contract, so this scenario is misapplied. Offered as a hedged alternative, and A says elsewhere that the old 4-year tier means 6400.
Cites "沪劳保发〔2000〕14号"; the correct number is 沪劳保保发〔2000〕14号 (minor).
Says 10号第九条 "只规定了病假工资的计算基数". This is incomplete: 第九条 also requires the employer to pay 假期工资 per the rules. A's own HR message does cite 第九条 for that duty.
"很多人（包括一些HR）还没更新" is unsupported colour.

The cited links (ft22.com mirror of the 10号 text, the rsj.sh.gov.cn 2025 Q&A, Ebner Stolz) cannot be verified from the answer. The Zhonglun link is real (opened). The ft22.com link is a non-official mirror.

States as fact that under the old rule "基数要先按正常工资的70%计算...8000×70%×80%=4480元，并非6400元". This contradicts the key (83号 tier at 4 years = 80% of 8000 = 6400). Per Zhonglun the 70% base applies only when the contract or collective contract specifies no wage, so it is wrong for an 8000 contract wage. The 3680 shortfall derived from it is also unsupported.

Says that if 应发 is about 2192 and 实发 is 800 after personal social insurance and housing fund, the company "是按最低线在发，能主张的差额会少很多". The majority view (14号 text, CMS) is that the minimum excludes personal contributions, so this still underpays. B concedes the minority reading without saying so.
The HR message and body never cite 309号第59条 or 10号第九条. They appear only as source links, and the 10号 link is not tied to 第九条's content.
The links (rsj.sh.gov.cn 83号 extension, 20260731 new measure, mohrss 309号) cannot be verified from the answer. The Zhonglun link is real (opened).
The deadlines in the HR message ("本周内", "下个工资发放日前") are invented demands, not legal rules. Minor.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise, say 83号 expired on 2026-08-15, and give 2740×80%=2192 and a 1392 shortfall. Both also give 6400/5600 as the contract or policy figure and point to 劳动监察 and 仲裁. A is stronger on the key's concrete points. It cites 309号第59条 and 10号第九条 in the HR message, spells out the 应发 versus 实发 check (800 as 应发 is plainly illegal, and the minimum excludes personal contributions), says an agreed ratio cannot be cut unilaterally, and asks for the calculation basis and the difference paid. B has no legal citation in the HR message, treats an 实发 of 800 as roughly the company paying the minimum, and states that the old 4-year figure is 4480 \"并非6400元\", which contradicts the key. A also carries a 4480 row, but only as one hedged contract scenario, and it says elsewhere that 4 years under the old tiers is 80%, about 6400. Neither explains the base exclusions or the ÷21.75 daily formula. B is shorter, while A runs long with a second HR reply and an evidence section, which costs A a little on concision but not enough to offset its accuracy lead.

added_claim_errors: "같은 법 제17조에 따라 연 20%의 지연이자": wrong citation. The delay interest comes from 근로기준법 제37조 and 시행령 제17조, not 퇴직급여법 제17조. The same wrong citation is repeated in the HR message.

"퇴직소득세·지방소득세 약 20만~25만 원": wrong. For about 1,024만~1,202만 with 4 service years, the tax including local tax is about 9.4만~14.1만 (I recomputed this). Also, with an IRP transfer nothing is withheld when the money is paid.
"3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금": outdated. Since 2026.9.18 the penalty under 제43조 is up to 5 years or 5천만 원 (minor, per the key).
"고용노동부와 법제처도 퇴직금 산정에 이 조항이 적용된다고 해석": no document number or link is given. The key supports the substance (법제처-26-0209).

"퇴직금 미지급은 3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금 (퇴직급여법 제44조)": outdated. Since 2026.9.18 it is 제43조, up to 5 years or 5천만 원. This also contradicts B's opening claim that it used the law in force in October 2026 (minor, per the key).
"퇴직소득세가 원천징수되어": imprecise. With an IRP transfer, which B itself describes, nothing is withheld when the money is paid (소득세법 제146조②).
HR message says "세전 약 1,020만 원": this contradicts B's own calculation (1,024만, up to 1,202만) and understates the claim to HR.
"법제처 해석(2026. 5. 26.)": I cannot verify the date, though a moleg.go.kr link is given and the key confirms 26-0209.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the company at the start: the deadline is 14 days, and an extension needs the worker's agreement. Both give the 1,024만~1,202만 range with the ordinary-wage floor and point to 1350 and a petition to the labour office. B's arithmetic matches the key exactly (1,158 days, 1,024만 and 1,202만), it cites the right source for the 20% delay interest (근로기준법 제37조), and it links its sources. A cites the delay interest to the wrong article (퇴직급여법 제17조), puts that wrong citation in the HR message, and roughly doubles the retirement tax (20만~25만 vs about 9만~14만). B's main weakness is that its HR message states 1,020만, below its own figures. Both cite the outdated 3-year/3천만 penalty.

added_claim_errors: The HR text and section 1 cite the delay interest under '근로자퇴직급여 보장법 제17조'. The 연 20% rate comes from 근로기준법 제37조 and 시행령 제17조, so the statute cited to the HR team is wrong.
'퇴직소득세·지방소득세 약 20만~25만 원을 빼면 실수령' is unsupported. An IRP transfer has no withholding at payment, and the key's estimate for a non-pension withdrawal is about 9.4만~14.1만.
'3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금' is the old penalty. Since 2026.9.18 it is 5 years or 50 million won under 제43조 (minor deduction).
The HR text says the 14 days run from '퇴사일 다음 날부터'. The statute counts from the day the payment ground arises, so the wording is imprecise.
'고용노동부와 법제처도 ... 해석합니다' gives no document number or link, so it is unverifiable as written (the key does support a 법제처 interpretation).
'실무에서는 두 방식이 갈리므로 1,200만 원을 기준으로 협의하시는 편이 유리' is unverifiable advice. The HR text also states 약 1,200만 원 as the amount, which is aggressive given the uncertainty over 통상임금.
It uses 1,157 days and 3.17 years and gets 약 1,023만, slightly off the key's 1,158 days and 약 1,024만 (rounding only).
'3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만 원 이하 벌금 (퇴직급여법 제44조)' is the old penalty. Since 2026.9.18 it is 5 years or 50 million won under 제43조 (minor deduction).
'퇴직소득세가 원천징수되어 실수령액은 조금 줄어듭니다' ignores that an IRP transfer means no withholding at payment. It is vague, with no wrong figure given.
'법제처 해석(2026. 5. 26.)' gives a date that is unverifiable, although the number 26-0209 matches the key.
'고용노동부 실무는 통상임금을 적용하는 쪽입니다' is unverifiable.
The HR text states the amount as 약 1,020만 원, the low end only. This is not an error, but it is weaker than the answer's own point that 1,202만 is arguable.
Section 5 on IRP omits the 300만 원 and under-55 conditions.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the company at the start: 14 days under 제9조제1항, an extension needs special circumstances plus agreement, and the deadline (about 10/4) is already past. B's figures match the key: 1,158 days, 약 1,024만 from the average wage, 126,316/day and 약 1,202만 from the 통상임금 floor, with 법제처 26-0209 named. A gives 1,157 days and 약 1,023만/1,200만, which is close but looser. A's HR text cites '퇴직급여법 제17조' for the delay interest, which is the wrong statute, and it gives an unsupported 20만~25만 tax figure. A's text also says '회사 사정이 있으실 수 있다는 점은 이해합니다', which comes close to reading as consent to a delay, and it leaves out IRP information. B's text is clean, requests 지급 예정일 and 산정 내역, and adds no wrong statute, though it also omits IRP and quotes only the lower amount. Both use the outdated 3년/3천만 원 penalty, and both cover 노동포털 or 지방관서 filing with 1350. B has fewer wrong specifics and better sourcing.

added_claim_errors: Step 2 "budget to spend roughly $1,240+" uses the 2025 $660 cap. For a 2026 plan year with a $680 cap, the required spend is $1,220 (minor, errs on the conservative side).
"about $1,220–$1,240 still forfeits": the range mixes the 2025 and 2026 caps. Only $1,220 is right for 2026 (minor).
Grace period "through March 15" is stated as fixed. March 15 is the legal maximum, and a plan may set a shorter period.
Run-out "often ~90 days after year-end" is an unverified typical figure, though it is hedged and plausible (judged from own knowledge).
"at most $660 of 2025 funds can move into 2026" uses the wrong plan year. The person's plan year ends Dec 31, 2026, and the 2026 cap is $680. B's own Proskauer link gives the 2026 limits.

"you can incur expenses through March 15, 2026 and still claim them against 2025 funds" has the wrong year: for this plan year the latest grace end is March 15, 2027. It also presents March 15 as fixed, when that is only the maximum.

The HR message says flatly '800元低于这个下限', assuming 800 is gross and never asking whether it is 应发 or 实发; it also sets deadlines ('本周内', '下个工资发放日前') that the user did not ask for.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start, explain that 83号 expired on 2026-08-15, give the 2192 yuan floor (2740×80%) and the 1392 yuan shortfall, and mention 劳动监察 and 仲裁. B gives 6400 and 5600 but frames them as a 'contract/policy only 80%' case, and it adds a 4480 'old-rule' figure from a 70% base multiplier. That figure contradicts the key's 6400 for the 83号 tiers, and the 70% base applies only when no wage is agreed, so it would confuse a user on an agreed 8000 salary. added_claim_errors: 「敷金から引くには修繕内容と費用の内訳を示す必要があります（民法622条の2）」: 622条の2 says what may be deducted (only money debts arising under the lease, such as unpaid rent). It sets no itemization requirement, so the citation is wrong.
「少額調停」: no formal procedure has this name (the procedure is 民事調停). The term is imprecise.

「国土交通省ガイドラインでは、壁紙（クロス）の張り替えは原則として貸主負担」 (repeated in the email): this overstates the guideline, which assigns cost by cause. Damage the tenant causes through negligence is the tenant's cost, so the management company could easily rebut this line.
「通常の使用によって生じた損耗・経年変化は含まれないのが判例・通説」: since 2020-04-01 this rule is written into 民法621条. Calling it case law and academic consensus misses the codification.
「少額訴訟（60万円以下）：…費用も数万円程度です」: overstated. For a claim of about 10万円 the filing fee is a few thousand yen (3,500 yen on paper under the current fees), not several tens of thousands.
「多くの場合、内訳を求められた時点で請求額は下がります」: a generalization with no support.

grade.reasons: Both answers catch the premise at the start and replace the acceptance email with a non-acceptance reply that asks for an itemized estimate. B is better on numbers: it states the 2万円 extra-claim risk and the 6-year life of wallpaper. But B's email tells the management company that the MLIT guideline makes wallpaper replacement the landlord's cost in principle. That overstates the guideline, and the other side could rebut it easily. A's email covers more of what the key asks for: sunburn as normal wear, partial repair, a breakdown with quantities, unit prices and depreciation, a joint inspection at move-out with photos, and 188. A's one error, citing 622条の2 as a requirement to itemize, sits in the explanation rather than in the email. Neither answer cites 民法621条 or the 2005 Supreme Court ruling, and neither demands return of the full 10万円 deposit.

added_claim_errors: 「敷金から引くには修繕内容と費用の内訳を示す必要があります（民法622条の2）」: 622条の2は敷金返還と、控除できるのは賃貸借に基づく金銭債務という趣旨の規定で、内訳提示義務を定めたものではない。条文趣旨の取り違え。
「少額調停・少額訴訟という手段もあります」: 「少額調停」は制度名として一般的でなく曖昧。少額訴訟は60万円以下で妥当。
メール案の「室内の写真は当方でも保管しております」: 利用者が写真を持っているとは限らない前提の挿入。
「これで金額が動く可能性が十分あります」: 根拠のない見込み。
「壁紙（クロス）の張り替えは原則として貸主負担」(管理会社宛メール案にも同旨): ガイドラインでは借主の故意・過失による損傷は借主負担(部分・減価考慮)。言い過ぎで、相手に反論されやすい。
「少額訴訟（60万円以下）：自分で提起でき、費用も数万円程度です」: 10万円前後の訴額なら手数料は数千円(新制度で書面3,500円・電子2,400円)。「数万円」は過大。
「多くの場合、内訳を求められた時点で請求額は下がります」「出せない請求は、根拠も怪しいことが多いです」: 根拠のない一般化で検証不能。
「民法90条で争える余地」: 通常損耗特約の争い方としては一般的でなく、補足的で根拠が弱い。

grade.reasons: Both answers refuse to write the acceptance email in their opening lines and supply a decline-and-request-itemisation reply, so both handle the trap well. Neither cites Civil Code Art. 621, the Supreme Court judgment of 16 Dec 2005, Annex 1 of the guideline, or the 20 April 2020 date, and neither demands the full 100,000 yen back. B hits more of the key's concrete numbers: the 6-year useful life with near-zero residual value at 7 years, the 20,000 yen extra-claim risk (120,000 - 100,000), and Consumer Contract Act Art. 10. Its email also states it does not agree to a lump-sum deduction from the deposit. It also gives no figure for depreciation and no 20,000 yen warning, and it defers settlement of the deposit instead of rejecting the deduction. B's errors are the overbroad "wallpaper replacement is the lessor's burden in principle" (repeated in the email) and the overstated small-claims cost. A's errors are the 622-2 mischaracterisation and the loose term "少額調停". B is slightly stronger on the key's specifics and slightly weaker on concision.

added_claim_errors: Ties the no-penalty delay to the 400 employees ('well over Medicare's 20-employee threshold... it lets you delay Part B'). Under 20 employees, says 'you'd need to enroll'. This is imprecise: the SEP doesn't depend on employer size; size only decides which plan pays first (minor, per key).
'you might need a Part D plan, and possibly Part B to get it': imprecise. Part D needs Part A or Part B, so someone who has premium-free Part A doesn't need Part B for it (hedged, minor).
'(some do; most don't)' on plans requiring Medicare at 65: an unsourced generalization, though plausible.

'When your coworker would be right: ... an employer under 20 employees ... missing your Initial Enrollment Period can trigger the 10%-per-year penalty': imprecise or wrong. The SEP for current-employment GHP coverage doesn't require 20+ employees; size only sets which plan pays first (minor, per key).

The question about whether the plan will 'carve out' benefits for Medicare-eligible employees who aren't enrolled suggests a 20+ employer may do this to active employees, but Medicare Secondary Payer rules generally forbid it (judged from my own knowledge; harmless as a question).

grade.reasons: Both answers open by rejecting the coworker's premise ('Don't enroll in Part B this month'). Both give the correct $202.90/month (about $2,435 a year) premium, the 8-month SEP and the HSA warning with 6-month Part A backdating. Both miss the IEP-end exception and the Medigap open-enrollment clock. A is tighter and includes the 2-month Part D window at retirement, which B lacks. B adds several correct, actionable specifics: the November 1 start if enrolled now, the 2024-MAGI IRMAA thresholds of $109,000 single and $218,000 joint, the $283 deductible, CMS-1763 for undoing an active enrollment, an explicit 'not retiree or COBRA' check with HR, the GEP fallback, and SHIP. Both slip slightly by tying the SEP to the 20-employee line, and B says it a little more explicitly. B's broader correct guidance outweighs its extra length, but only slightly.

added_claim_errors: Plan requires Medicare at 65 ('some do; most don't'): the frequency claim is unverifiable.
Call SSA at 1-800-772-1213 and ask to withdraw the application before it takes effect: the number is right, but whether withdrawal is possible is stated flatly and is not checkable from the packet.
Cites Medicare.gov and Federal Register (govinfo FR-2025-11-19) links as sources: checkable links given, but page contents not confirmed here.
'Medicare.gov's sign-up tool asks exactly the 20-employee question': claim about a tool's behavior, unverifiable from the packet.

Asks whether the plan 'carves out' benefits for Medicare-eligible non-enrollees and says to enroll if it does: for a 20+ employer's active employees such carve-outs are generally not allowed under Medicare Secondary Payer rules, so the concern is misleading (my own knowledge).
Pay stubs/W-2s as backup alongside CMS-L564: unverifiable, and not part of the key.
Terminating Part B with CMS-1763, with re-enrollment restricted and premiums not refunded: plausible and I believe the form is right, but not covered by the key.
'Part B starts November 1, 2026' assumes the current month is October 2026 (matches the key, but the request gives no date).

grade.reasons: Both answers open by rejecting the premise ('Don't enroll in Part B this month'). Both give the 8-month penalty-free window, 20+ employee primary-payer status, the $202.90 premium (about $2,435 a year), the HSA/Part A warning with 6-month retroactivity, the decline-Part-B step for Social Security recipients, creditable drug coverage, and CMS-L564. Its HR checklist explicitly excludes COBRA and retiree coverage, its HSA advice is more actionable (stop contributions first), it adds the General Enrollment Period fallback, and its 'when your coworker would be right' section matches the key's side-claim traps. added_claim_errors: 劳部发〔1997〕271号「第四条」(holiday 300%, no comp leave) and「第五条」(cycle 150%, holidays per Art 44(3)): the content is real, but the article numbers look shifted by one; to my knowledge these are items 3 and 4 of that reply letter

added_claim_errors: 「7年住んでいるなら残存価値はゼロ、つまり更新の必要があっても借主負担分は生じません」: the guideline sets the residual value at 1 yen, not zero, and a tenant who caused intentional or negligent damage can still be charged labour and work costs after the useful life ends. A minor overstatement.
「サインは「内容を確認した」以上の意味を持ちません」: overclaim. Signing is assent to the contract terms; a clause that names the wallpaper specifically can be valid under the 2005 Supreme Court test.

The link labelled 「国民生活センターの相談事例」 points to a kokusen 'hanrei' (court-case digest) path archived on WARP. I fetched it and got no content, so its label and its support for the claim are unverifiable.
The link labelled 「国交省ガイドライン関連の解説」 goes to a private explainer site (kurashitokanri.jpm.jp), not the MLIT guideline. It is offered as support for a guideline claim but is not an official source.

grade.reasons: Both answers decline the acceptance email at the start and give a non-acceptance reply that cites Civil Code Article 621 and the guideline's treatment of sunlight discoloration. A explains the special-clause requirement more accurately: the scope must be specifically explained and agreed. A also spells out the risk of accepting (a 20,000 yen shortfall plus a written admission of debt), and its email is a firm refusal that asks for a breakdown, the clause and the depreciation basis. A's main gaps are that it never demands the full 100,000 yen deposit back and never states the rule that a charge is limited to the damaged area (one wall face at most). added_claim_errors: 「7年住んでいるなら残存価値はゼロ」: 定額法には下限の1円があり、正確には「1円（≒0%）」。軽微な不正確さ。
「書面で同意すると債務を認めた記録が残り、後から覆すのが難しくなります」: 法的帰結を一般論として断定しており、出典なし（根拠は検証不能）。
「相談実績が非常に多い分野です」: 数字・出典なしの主張で検証不能。
日焼けの黄ばみに経過年数の減価計算（耐用年数6年、残存価値ゼロ）を当てて説明している。日焼けは通常損耗であり計算以前に負担義務がない、という整理にはなっていない（軽微）。
「サインは『内容を確認した』以上の意味を持ちません」: 署名した契約書には拘束力があり、言い過ぎ。特約が明記されていれば別になりうる。
国交省ガイドラインの根拠として、民間の管理会社系ブログ（kurashitokanri.jpm.jp）を「国交省ガイドライン関連の解説」として挙げている。一次資料ではなく、内容を確認できなかった。

「民法621条は…（2017年改正で明文化）」: 改正の公布年としては正しいが、施行は2020年4月1日で、施行日や旧法契約の扱いには触れていない。
「少額でも相談は無料です」: 188の通話料などの条件に触れておらず、断定がやや強め（軽微）。

grade.reasons: Both answers refuse to write the acceptance email at the start and correct the premise: 民法621条, 日焼けは経年変化で貸主負担, 耐用年数6年で残存価値ほぼゼロ. Both supply a non-accepting reply that asks for the 内訳 and the contract clause. B's reply also cites the MLIT guideline, asks for return of the 敷金10万円, and mentions 立会い photos and 188, and B is shorter. B overstates that signing means no more than having read the contract, and it leans on secondary links I could not verify, so it loses on honesty. B's email is closer to the key's recommended reply and the answer is tighter, but A is more reliable, so the margin is slight.

added_claim_errors: Attributes the expiry of both 83号 and 14号 to the 上海人社局答复; per the key, the official reply confirmed only 83号, and 14号's expiry is a presumption with no explicit official statement. Overstated.

Opening line "如果劳动合同或公司制度沿用旧上海口径，可能是 4480 元" maps the old Shanghai approach to 8000×70%×80%. The 70% base was only a fallback when no wage was agreed, and with an agreed 8000 wage the old rules gave 6400. Section 2 adds that condition, but the headline figure misleads.

Says in the present tense that the base is 70% of normal wage when the contract is silent. The key cites 10号第九条 only as contract wage with a 2740 floor, so whether the new rules keep the 70% fallback is unverifiable.

Table row "制度照搬旧上海算法（先按实得工资70%，再按4—6年80%）" = 4480 calls a 70% base the old Shanghai algorithm. Under the old rules the 70% base (of 正常出勤月工资, not 实得工资) applied only when no wage was agreed at all, and with an agreed 8000 wage the result was 6400. Misleading.
The HR letter attributes the 80%-of-minimum floor to "上海现行规定". The floor comes from national 劳部发〔1995〕309号第59条, not a current Shanghai rule. Minor misattribution.

grade.reasons: Both answers get the core right: 83号 and 14号 lapsed on 2026-08-15, the September floor is 2740×80%=2192 (1392 short of 800), 6400 applies only if the contract or company rules say so, and both name 12333, labour inspection and arbitration. Both also add a questionable 4480 figure (70% base × 80%); A at least states that the 70% base applies only when no wage was agreed. B corrects the '公司说了算' premise more directly in its first line and is tighter. A covers more of the key: it raises 应发 vs 实发 and asks HR about it, cites 309号第59条 by name in the letter, and asks for base, ratio and the rule relied on. B never raises 应发/实发 and its letter cites only vague '上海现行规定'. A's better coverage of points 6 and 7 outweighs B's edge on trap handling and concision.

States as fact that 沪劳保保发〔2000〕14号 expired on 2026-08-15. The key says this is only inferred, and the official reply covers 83号.
"网上很多答案还在写旧标准，是因为那些页面发布在2026年8月15日之前" is speculation about why online answers differ, with no source.

The medical-period remark ("1个月病假在医疗期内，公司不能仅以病假为由解除劳动合同") is directionally right but gives no N+2 figure or statutory basis.
Table row "制度照搬旧上海算法（先按实得工资70%，再按4—6年80%）= 4480" is unverifiable and conflicts with the key's 6400 for 83号 tiers. It also never says when the base would be 8000 and not 70%.
States as fact that the 14号 file expired on 2026-08-15, though the key says this is only inferred.

The closing "依据" list gives links, but the text cites no instrument by number except 309号第59条 in the link label. The letter itself cites no instrument by number, so the legal basis cannot be checked from the text.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise, state that 83号 and 14号 expired on 2026-08-15, and calculate the legal floor as 2740 x 80% = 2192 yuan, which is 1392 yuan short of 800. Both also add a 4480 figure framed as the old Shanghai approach, which muddies the key's 6400 under the 83号 tiers; neither calls it a legal minimum. A's letter asks whether 800 is 应发 or 实发, names the 309号第59条 basis, and requests basis, ratio, institutional grounds and back pay. It omits the 10号第九条 citation and the wage statement. added_claim_errors: "회사가 사실상 도산했다면 근로복지공단 소액체당금": uses the old name (renamed 간이대지급금 in 2021), and the 도산 condition is wrong. 간이대지급금 does not require insolvency.
"신청은 퇴사 다음 날부터 12개월 이내": imprecise. The 12 months is the 수급기간 (제48조), so a late claim loses days. A 150-day entitlement needs filing within about 208 days.
"구직촉진수당(월 50만원, 최대 6개월)": the 2026 amount is unverified (the key does not penalize it, but it needs checking). It is listed as a source alongside 구직급여 even though receiving 구직급여 can exclude it.
"워크넷 구직등록 후 관할 고용센터에 수급자격을 신청": wrong. 워크넷 has ended and was merged into 고용24.

"퇴사 후 14일 안에 청산하지 않으면 바로 진정할 수 있습니다": misleading. Wages already overdue can be reported right away, with no need to wait 14 days.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start and cite 시행규칙 별표 2 (2개월 이상 임금체불 within the year before leaving). added_claim_errors: Says 劳部发〔1994〕503号 and 京劳社资发〔2003〕157号 both require filing with the 区人社局. Only 157号 (Art. 15) says that; 503号 leaves local approval to provincial rules. Minor misattribution.
Table shows 413.79 × 300% × 3 = 3,724.14, but 413.79 × 9 = 3,724.11. The figure comes from the unrounded daily wage. The key accepts either, so this is only a small internal inconsistency.

"法定节假日的工时不计入综合计算周期的总工时" is unsourced and unverifiable. 157号 Art. 8 (I opened the beijing.gov.cn text) says "其中法定休假日安排职工工作的…", which reads as holiday hours counting inside the period total. The claim is doubtful.

grade.reasons: Both answers reject the 'signed so nothing can be done' premise. Both say approval is what counts and that holiday work earns 300% even with approval. Both split the days correctly into 3 statutory holidays and 4 rest days, and both reach the right figures: 3,724.14 + 3,310.34 = 7,034.48, paid on top of the 9,000 salary. A puts both refutations in its opening and stays compact, with almost no unverifiable additions. It does not name 劳动合同法 Art. 26 and leaves out the 9月20日/10月10日 make-up workdays. B covers more of the key: Art. 26/27, the make-up days, verifying the approval, free arbitration, and time limits. Taken together, A's concision and cleaner claims slightly outweigh B's extra completeness.

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start (no approval means the 综合工时 clause has no effect, and signing does not waive overtime pay). Both also state that 1 to 3 October is 300% even with an approval, and both reach 3,724.14 + 3,310.34 = 7,034.48 yuan. I recomputed the arithmetic: 9000/21.75 = 413.79, and every figure checks out in both answers. A cites 人社部发〔2025〕2号 for 21.75, as the key does. It is much tighter and carries fewer unverifiable source claims, though it skips the 9/20 and 10/10 working days and the free-arbitration and verify-the-approval steps. Coverage and concision roughly cancel out, so A wins slightly on concision and honesty. I judged the unverified claims from my own knowledge and did not open any links.

added_claim_errors: 「店側が変更できるのは本当に忙しくて回らないときだけです」: a loose paraphrase of the seasonal-change right. The legal test is 事業の正常な運営を妨げる場合, and the key says that simply being busy is not a reason, so framing it as busyness is imprecise.
「付与日や日数は就業規則にも書いてあるので」: 休暇 is a required item in 就業規則 (Art. 89), but the answer cannot know that this store's rules spell out the grant date and number of days. Unverifiable, minor.

added_claim_errors: "risks forfeiting roughly $1,220–$1,240": the $1,240 figure uses the 2025 $660 cap, which does not apply to a 2026 plan year (minor). The line also leaves out the no-feature branch, where all $1,900 is at risk.

"the unused balance on December 31 is forfeited" / "$1,220+ evaporates on January 1": imprecise. Forfeiture is measured after the run-out period, and 2026 claims filed during run-out still count. B elsewhere says run-out is for submitting 2026 receipts.

"spending $1,500 on stuff you wouldn't otherwise buy to save $680 is a loss": muddled. FSA money is already contributed, so spending it before forfeiture costs nothing extra out of pocket, and the $1,500 and $680 figures do not match any branch.

added_claim_errors: "(Part D is 63 days.)" and "Enroll in Part D or a Medicare Advantage plan within 63 days if your drug coverage isn't creditable": these mix up two rules. 63 days is the coverage gap that triggers the penalty. The enrollment window after employer coverage ends is 2 full months, and if the current drug coverage is not creditable, the penalty is already building.

Ties the no-penalty delay to the 400-employee size ("your coworker's penalty warning doesn't apply to you at 400 employees"). The SEP does not depend on employer size; the 20-employee line only decides who pays first. Minor imprecision.
"six-month Medigap open enrollment window (in most states)": the 6-month Medigap open enrollment is a federal right, so the 'most states' hedge is imprecise. Minor; state rules were not checked.

"That lets you delay Part B with no late-enrollment penalty" is attributed to the company being over the 20-employee threshold. The SEP does not depend on employer size; size only decides who pays first. Minor imprecision.

grade.reasons: Both answers open by correcting the coworker's premise. Both say Part B can wait with no penalty under the 8-month SEP, flag COBRA, give a sound HR checklist, and include the HSA caveat on Part A. A covers more of the key. It gives the correct 2026 premium ($202.90/month, about $2,435 a year), says Part B would only be secondary coverage, notes that the Medigap open enrollment starts with Part B, and says Part D can wait with creditable coverage. B never gives the premium or mentions Medigap, and only touches on Part D through the creditable-coverage notice. B is tighter and has fewer side errors; A muddles the Part D timing by giving '63 days' as the enrollment window. Neither answer states the exception for a job or coverage that ends during the IEP. Both handle retirement steps only loosely, with no CMS-L564 and no CMS-40B. Taken together, A's fuller coverage outweighs B's concision by a small margin.

added_claim_errors: "Enroll in Part D or a Medicare Advantage plan within 63 days if your drug coverage isn't creditable": the condition is inverted. The window after coverage ends applies when creditable coverage is lost; non-creditable drug coverage means Part D should have been taken earlier. The key says 2 full months.
"Don't enroll in Part B, Medicare Advantage, or Part D this month" is unconditional; if the plan's drug coverage turns out not to be creditable, waiting on Part D risks a permanent penalty.
"Your coworker's penalty warning doesn't apply to you at 400 employees" ties the penalty exemption to employer size. The SEP does not depend on size; size decides who pays first (imprecise, minor).
The KFF, ARPI and Federal Register/govinfo links are given as sources with nothing checkable beyond the URLs. ARPI is not an official source. Unverifiable.
"Part B ... covering little your plan doesn't already cover" and "mostly duplicates" depend on the plan and are asserted without evidence (minor).
The 20-employee threshold is presented as what "lets you delay Part B with no late-enrollment penalty". The SEP is not size-conditional; size decides who pays first (imprecise, minor).
Medicare.gov source links are cited as the basis for the answer, with no way to verify they were consulted. Unverifiable.
"Call Social Security at 1-800-772-1213 and ask about withdrawing it before it takes effect": the number is correct, but the withdrawal procedure is not covered by the key and is unverified.
"Enrolling now [in Part A] is often sensible" omits the 10-year work-history condition and that Part A pays second (minor omission, not an error).

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start. grade.reasons: Both answers correct the baited premise in the opening lines: approval is what counts, signing does not waive it, and 1-3 October is paid at 300% even with approval. Both get the scenario A amounts right (3724.14 + 3310.34 = 7034.48 yuan, paid on top of the 9000 salary), and both note that comp time can offset the 4 rest days. A is stronger on the key's specifics: it cites Labor Law Art 39 and 157 Arts 3-4, bases the 21.75 divisor on 人社部发〔2025〕2号, and says to check the approval with the district bureau. It does not invent a scenario B 150% amount. B gives no article for the Beijing rule and no basis for the 21.75 divisor. added_claim_errors: '회사가 사실상 도산했다면 근로복지공단 소액체당금도 확인' — the scheme has been called 간이대지급금 since 2021, and it does not require the company to be insolvent (that condition belongs to 도산대지급금). Outdated name and wrong condition.

'국민취업지원제도 — 구직촉진수당(월 50만원, 최대 6개월)' listed as a living-cost source next to 실업급여. Someone receiving 구직급여 can be excluded from the allowance, so presenting it as an extra income stream is misleading. The answer does not say outright that both can be paid at once, and the amount is not penalized (judged from own knowledge and the key).
'신청은 퇴사 다음 날부터 12개월 이내' — imprecise. The 12 months is the 수급기간, so a late application loses benefit days. It is not simply a deadline to file (key).

'7~9월 석 달이면 이 요건을 넘고' — overstated. Eligibility depends on the total days paid late or unpaid reaching 60, not on the number of late months. Three months each paid a few days late may not qualify (key).
'2년 근무면 150일분이 나오고' — leaves out the age condition: claimants aged 50 or over, or with a disability, get 180 days (key).
'이직일 다음 날부터 12개월 안에 신청해야 하고' — imprecise. The 12 months is the 수급기간, so filing late loses benefit days. It is not just a deadline to file (key).

grade.reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start with 별표 2. B also says that wages paid late (지연 지급) count, which matters here because this person's pay was late, not necessarily unpaid. B overstates by saying three months is enough, without the 60-day criterion, though the key counts that as a minor fault. Neither answer mentions 생계비 융자 or the age-based 180 days.

added_claim_errors: '근로복지공단 소액체당금' is the old name of 간이대지급금, and the condition '회사가 사실상 도산했다면' is wrong: 간이대지급금 can be claimed while the business is still operating.
'어느 기준으로 봐도 요건에 해당할 가능성이 높고' never states the 60-day total-delay-days criterion; hedged by '아예 못 받으셨다면', so low severity.
Lists 구직촉진수당 (월 50만원, 최대 6개월) in the same ordered list as 구직급여 without saying it can be excluded while receiving 구직급여; the cue '자격을 확인하세요' softens it.

'2년 근무면 150일분이 나오고' leaves out that age 50 or over, or a disability, gives 180 days.

The imaeil article and 1350 links are cited as the basis; they are checkable links, but I did not open them and cannot say how far they support the text.

added_claim_errors: "The Part B late-enrollment penalty ... applies to people who go without creditable coverage": wrong framing. The Part B SEP depends on a group health plan based on current employment, not on 'creditable coverage' (a Part D term). Retiree or COBRA coverage can be creditable for drugs and still not protect against the Part B penalty.
Ties the no-penalty delay to the plan being 'well above the 20-employee threshold': imprecise. Employer size decides which plan pays first, not whether the SEP exists (minor).
Says to apply at retirement with 'CMS-40B plus CMS-L564' and gives no Part A caveat. CMS-40B is only for people who already have Part A, and A itself tells HSA holders to defer Part A.
"CMS-L564, completed by your employer": partly wrong. The enrollee fills in Section A and the employer fills in Section B.
"Sign up for Part D within 63 days": imprecise. The Part D SEP runs 2 full months after coverage ends; 63 days is the gap that triggers the penalty (minor).

"Well over Medicare's 20-employee threshold. That lets you delay Part B with no late-enrollment penalty": imprecise. Employer size is not a condition of the SEP; it decides which plan pays first. B's later under-20 explanation is right in practice (minor).

grade.reasons: Both answers catch the bad premise at the start and correctly say the asker can delay Part B through the 8-month SEP. A also recommends CMS-40B with no caveat about needing Part A, says the employer completes CMS-L564 alone, and gives a 63-day Part D deadline. A is stronger on the retirement paperwork (it names CMS-L564) and on Part D waiting without penalty, but B has fewer errors overall.

Retirement steps omit CMS-L564, CMS-40B and the Part D 2-month window, offering only an HR letter. This is an omission, not an error.
